# INCIDB — The Skincare & Cosmetics INCI Database

> A normalised relational snapshot of cosmetic ingredient labels: 18,583 products, 5,925 brands, 46,973 distinct canonical INCI names, 318,758 ordered product→ingredient composition links, and a 55,426-row `ingredient_name_map` recording how every raw label token was resolved to a canonical name. Product/brand/composition data from Open Beauty Facts (ODbL); ingredient enrichment (functions, CAS, EC numbers, chemical descriptions, Annex II–VI membership, restrictions) joined on exact canonical name from the European Commission CosIng inventory. Where a source has no value the column is NULL — nothing is defaulted or inferred. Snapshot 2026.09.

## Measured Enrichment Coverage (do not round up)
Coverage is reported two ways, because they differ by an order of magnitude and only quoting one would mislead:
- **CosIng match:** 11.0% of the 46,973 distinct canonical names; 82.5% of the 318,758 ingredient occurrences on product labels (link-weighted).
- **`functions` (CosIng vocabulary, multi-valued):** 10.9% of distinct names; 81.5% link-weighted.
- **`cas_number`:** 8.3% of distinct names; 76.4% link-weighted.
- **`chemical_description`:** 8.5% of distinct names, 3,965 distinct values.
- **`is_common_allergen`:** 99 names flagged, from the EU Annex III fragrance-allergen list (Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/1545). The US FDA has not yet published its MoCRA fragrance-allergen list, so no US flag exists here.
- **`comedogenic_rating`:** 145 ingredients rated 0–5, transcribed from Fulton JE Jr., J Soc Cosmet Chem 1989;40:321–333 (Table I); NULL elsewhere.
- **`is_fungal_acne_trigger`:** 270 rule-derived flags (C11–C24 fatty acids and their esters, polysorbates 20/40/60/80, applied only to CosIng-matched ingredients). A heuristic, not a measured property. Basis: DOI 10.3389/fcimb.2020.00112, DOI 10.1093/femsyr/foaf043.

Reason for the gap between the two views: a real-world label corpus contains far more distinct strings (botanical variants, multilingual spellings, marketing tokens) than any regulatory inventory lists, but the ingredients that actually fill label slots are the ones CosIng covers.

## Capabilities & Specs
- **Tables:** `products`, `brands`, `ingredients`, `product_ingredients`, `ingredient_name_map`.
- **Formats:** pipe-delimited UTF-8 CSV (`|`) and Apache Parquet (`pyarrow`).
- **Canonicalisation:** raw label token → canonical INCI name via an explicit method recorded per row (`exact`, `cleaned`, `typo_map`, `percent_stripped`, `paren_stripped`, `synonym_map`, `slash_variant`, `split`, `unresolved`). The map ships with the data so every decision is auditable.
- **Sources:** Open Beauty Facts (product corpus, ODbL) and European Commission CosIng (ingredient enrichment, EU open data).
- **Attribution:** "Product data © Open Beauty Facts contributors", licensed ODbL v1.0 (attribution + share-alike). "Contains data from the European Commission CosIng database."
- **Free sample:** 200 products with their brands, 1,109 referenced ingredients, their composition links and name-map rows. The draw is a seeded uniform random sample of the products whose ingredient lists are at least 80% CosIng-matched, so it reads better than the corpus average — plan against the corpus figures above.
- **Product:** INCIDB Complete — $79 one-time, all 5 tables in both formats plus the build report, instant Stripe checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/3cIfZi5t6fzwazV1E43840g
- **What the price buys:** the normalisation, canonicalisation, joining and measurement, plus hosted instant delivery. Not exclusive rights to the underlying data, which remains ODbL.
